claims.text: The starting material is nominally equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Local compositional partitioning occurs in HfNbTaTiZr and contributes to microstructural heterogeneity.
Differential thermal expansion generates internal mismatch stresses in HfNbTaTiZr.
Mismatch-induced internal stresses govern high-temperature creep in HfNbTaTiZr.
Mismatch-induced internal stresses govern the evolution of elastic moduli and hardness after cold rolling or aging.
In situ high-temperature diffraction can track lattice-strain evolution under load.
In situ diffraction and associated modeling can determine temperature-dependent elastic moduli.
Diffraction peak shifts and lattice-parameter changes can quantify the proposed internal mismatch stresses.
Thermal mismatch and compositional segregation create a persistent internal stress state that changes the balance among dislocation slip, climb, and precipitation.
Precipitate lattice misfit and stable precipitates can contribute to elevated-temperature strengthening and creep resistance.
Samples with stronger mismatch signatures will exhibit greater creep resistance.
Samples with stronger mismatch signatures will retain more strength after rolling.
Samples with stronger mismatch signatures will show sharper temperature-dependent changes in elastic moduli.
A fully homogenized reference will have less partitioning and weaker mismatch-stress development than an as-cast reference.
The homogenized reference will exhibit lower high-temperature strength and less temperature-sensitive elastic moduli.
Below approximately 600 °C, limited diffusion produces negligible new precipitation or ordering and diminishes mismatch-driven effects.
Above approximately 1250 °C, diffusion and dislocation climb dominate creep, making mismatch stresses less significant.
A lack of correlation between measured mismatch stresses and elastic, plastic, creep, or hardness changes would falsify mismatch stress as the unifying mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes cold-rolling-related hardness behavior, which occurs below 600 °C, to mismatch-induced activity, while the boundary broadly says mismatch-driven effects are diminished below about 600 °C. The fields do not distinguish deformation-generated residual mismatch from diffusion-dependent precipitation mismatch.
